Corporate Security at Ramp owns the identity and access layer for the company: Okta, Google Workspace, the SaaS applications behind them, and the governance that decides who holds what. You will report to the Corporate Security lead and work closely with IT, Security Engineering, AI DevX, and the Data team.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Own Terraform for identity services: Okta applications, authorization servers, authentication policies, groups and group rules, and SCIM provisioning

- Design and operate custom authorization servers, including audiences, scopes, claims, and access policies for internal services and AI agents

- Implement app-to-app and agent access through Cross App Access (XAA) and ID-JAG, so delegated access is brokered and governed by the IdP rather than granted user by user

- Own our IGA platform: the entitlement catalog, ownership, access requests, time-bound grants, and certifications

- Build the agentic workflow that takes a team from "I have a new group of people who need access to X" to a defined, owned, and governed entitlement, with the Terraform and IGA changes opened for review

- Build identity graphs with ISPM tooling to target overprivileged and long-standing access across human and non-human identities

- Build the identity data lake behind an on-call agent that can explain events like a User Not Assigned Application error in Okta before the employee opens a ticket

WHAT YOU NEED

- 6+ years in identity engineering or IAM, including operational ownership of Okta or an equivalent identity provider at scale

- Deep understanding of OAuth 2.0, OIDC, SAML, and SCIM, including how custom authorization servers issue and enforce aud, scope, and claims

- Working knowledge of how XAA and ID-JAG work under the hood, including token exchange and JWT bearer grants

- Experience with ISPM or identity graph tooling, and turning its findings into automated remediation

- Experience owning an IGA platform or building the equivalent in-house

- Terraform experience managing identity providers, including module design, state, and CI

- Programming in Python or Go, with experience building against platform APIs

Positron AI is building next-generation AI inference accelerators designed from the ground up for low-latency, high-throughput large language model inference. Chips built for the training era keep running into two walls at inference time: memory bandwidth and chip-to-chip networking. We designed our architecture to break through both. Our first-generation Atlas systems are already in production on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. Asimov, our first custom ASIC, takes that architecture to silicon. In simulations, Asimov delivers several times more tokens per dollar and tokens per watt than leading GPUs, at a fraction of the power. Our team includes engineers from Groq, Lambda, NVIDIA, Meta, F5, and many other industry leaders.

Role Overview

Running one AI model across many chips is a distributed systems problem: a host and many chips exchanging data over links, waiting on each other, and failing in ways no single chip would. As a Senior Distributed Systems Engineer, you will help us simulate that system before the hardware exists. You will work with the chip modeling, SDK, and runtime teams to build the simulators that stand in for the host, the links, and the protocols between chips.

This role is about building and scaling simulation infrastructure, not testing someone else's code. You will own the software architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack, decide how much fidelity each layer needs, and keep it fast enough that distributed software is exercised every day in CI.

Architecture and Scale

• Own the architecture of the multi-chip simulation stack as new chips, interconnects, and deployment topologies arrive.

• Compose simulators of different fidelity (fast functional, cycle-level, and hardware emulation) into one coherent multi-chip simulation.

• Scale the simulation from a few chips to full racks while keeping runs fast enough for daily use in CI.

Correlation and Quality

• Correlate simulated behavior against emulation and hardware measurements, with regression coverage and clear documentation of assumptions and limitations.

• 5+ years of experience as a distributed systems engineer building and operating software that coordinates many machines or accelerators through RPC, message passing, consensus, or collective communication.

• A strong understanding of the failure modes of distributed software, including races, partial failure, ordering and consistency, timeouts and retries, back-pressure, and deadlock.

• Demonstrated experience debugging timing-dependent bugs across hosts, NICs, or accelerators using traces and logs.

• Experience building simulators, emulators, or test harnesses for distributed or networked systems is strongly preferred.
